# PLAN — iteration 1

## Current state assessment

The baseline passes simulation and has positive hold slack (0.091 ns), but setup fails at WNS −0.931 ns. The reported critical path reads `out_data` through distributed RAM from `rd_ptr`; its OBUF and clock insertion contribute most of the delay. The incumbent uses 13 LUTs and 6 FFs. The top requires `// @latency 1`; preserve its observable FIFO behavior and all supported `WIDTH` and `DEPTH` values.

## Hypothesis

Changing the FIFO storage to a shift-on-pop register array should drive `out_data` directly from the head register, improving the output timing path at the cost of more FFs and potentially changing LUT use.

## Instruction for generator

In `sync_fifo_core`, replace the dynamically indexed memory read with a register array whose entries hold queued words in order: shift entries toward the head on each pop, then write accepted input at the post-pop tail, with push taking priority if both updates target the same entry. Drive `out_data` from the head register and retain the occupancy-based `out_valid`, combinational `in_ready`, explicit capacity behavior, and synchronous reset of queue state. Preserve full simultaneous pop/push, stable head data during stalls, minimum transfer age, and the current top’s `// @latency 1` annotation; keep `sync_fifo_core` defined and live-reached from `sync_fifo`.
